Bush]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Texas sidebar}} The '''1994 Texas gubernatorial election''' was held on November 8, 1994, to elect the [[governor of Texas|governor of the U.S. state of Texas]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Governor [[Ann Richards]] was defeated in her bid for re-election by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee and future president [[George W. Bush]], the son of former President [[George H. W. Bush]]. Before the election, Richards had a high approval rating due to the strength of the state economy. However, Bush's campaigning on cultural and religious issues resonated with many Texan voters, and the race was considered a tossup on election day. On election day, Bush carried 188 of the state's 254 counties, while Richards carried 66. This marks the most recent time a Democratic candidate for governor has carried [[Briscoe County, Texas|Briscoe]], [[Hall County, Texas|Hall]], [[Cottle County, Texas|Cottle]], [[Hardeman County, Texas|Hardeman]], [[Knox County, Texas|Knox]], [[Baylor County, Texas|Baylor]], [[Dickens County, Texas|Dickens]], [[Jones County, Texas|Jones]], [[Nolan County, Texas|Nolan]], [[Mitchell County, Texas|Mitchell]], [[Clay County, Texas|Clay]], [[Palo Pinto County, Texas|Palo Pinto]], [[Comanche County, Texas|Comanche]], [[Menard County, Texas|Menard]], [[Fannin County, Texas|Fannin]], [[Delta County, Texas|Delta]], [[Rains County, Texas|Rains]], [[Camp County, Texas|Camp]], [[San Augustine County, Texas|San Augustine]], [[Sabine County, Texas|Sabine]], [[Tyler County, Texas|Tyler]], [[Orange County, Texas|Orange]], [[Caldwell County, Texas|Caldwell]], [[Galveston County, Texas|Galveston]], [[Robertson County, Texas|Robertson]], [[Milam County, Texas|Milam]], [[Limestone County, Texas|Limestone]], and [[San Patricio County, Texas|San Patricio]] counties. Exit polls revealed that Bush won overwhelmingly among white voters (69% to 31%) while Richards performed well among African Americans (83% to 15%) and Latinos (75% to 25%). Despite the loss of Richards, the Democratic Party was more successful in other statewide offices: Lieutenant Governor [[Bob Bullock]], Attorney General [[Dan Morales]], Land Commissioner [[Garry Mauro]] and Comptroller [[John Sharp (Texas politician)|John Sharp]] all won reelection. The Democrats would not win statewide office in Texas again until [[Gina Hinojosa]] was elected Governor in 2026. Bush's victory was one of the most notable in the 1994 [[Republican Revolution]], as he was one of four candidates to defeat an incumbent governor that cycle. This was, [[2026 Texas gubernatorial election|until 2026]], the last time an incumbent governor of Texas lost re-election. ==Primaries== ===Republican=== {{Election box begin|title = Republican primary}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link |party = Republican Party (United States) |candidate = [[George W.
